newsitem.title: GERMANY: German co-ops defend EU beef/milk regimes.
newsitem.headline: German co-ops defend EU beef/milk regimes.

text.p: The organisation grouping German farm cooperatives (DRV) said it would seek to preserve European Union support for the beef and milk markets.
EU intervention buying was needed to prevent further beef price slumps in the ongoing mad cow crisis, DRV president Joerg Brixner said in a statement distributed during annual meetings.
"The (recent) fifth case of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) in Germany has had drastic consequences for our beef sales," he said.
"Not only did the domestic market collapse, but Russia, Belarus, Poland, Hungary, Croatia, Bosnia and Serbia temporarily banned beef imports from Germany."
He hoped exports would resume after the Bonn government intervened to allay importers' fears.
DRV was committed to consumer protection and would support any government measures to prevent further cases.
In the milk sector, DRV wished to keep those elements of the current quota system which would stabilise prices and market patterns.
Quotas are due to expire in March 2000 and the EU needs to examine possibilities for reforming policy.
"Any abrupt liberalisation of the regime would exceed the adaptability of German producers," Brixner said.
